LeadRequest.title: LeadRequest
LeadRequest.description: Represents a lead request submitted via the /devis (quote) page.

id.description: Unique identifier for the lead request. (Primary Key)

fullName.description: Full name of the person submitting the request.

email.description: Email address of the person submitting the request.

phone.description: Phone number of the person submitting the request.

company.description: Company name of the person submitting the request (if applicable).

serviceOfInterest.description: The specific service the lead is interested in.

message.description: Additional message or details provided by the lead.

submissionDate.description: Date and time when the lead request was submitted.

ipAddress.description: IP address of the user submitting the form (for spam prevention).

definition.description: Stores lead requests submitted via the /devis page.  Each document represents a single lead request.

params.name: leadRequestId
params.description: Unique identifier for the lead request document.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to store lead requests submitted via the /devis page. A single collection, `lead_requests`, is used to store all lead request documents. Each document within the collection represents a single lead request and contains all the relevant information. This structure promotes simplicity and ease of querying, as all lead requests are stored in a single, flat collection.

Authorization Independence: Since all lead requests are stored in a single collection without hierarchical relationships, there's no need for authorization checks based on parent documents. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls in security rules, enabling atomic operations and simplifying debugging.

QAPs (Rules are not Filters): Storing all lead requests in a single collection facilitates secure `list` operations. Security rules can be implemented to restrict access based on specific criteria, ensuring that only authorized users or processes can access the lead request data.
